text: Sandra Douglass Morgan, born on April 10, 1978, is an American attorney and football executive who serves as the president of the Las Vegas Raiders in the National Football League. She is the first Black and Asian woman to hold the position of NFL team president. Prior to this role, she served on the Nevada State Athletic Commission and was chairwoman of the Nevada Gaming Control Board. Her father, Gilbert, is a Black American retired United States Air Force veteran, and her mother, Kil Cha, is Korean. Raised in Las Vegas, Douglass Morgan graduated from Eldorado High School, earned a bachelor's degree in political science and communication from the University of Nevada, Reno in 1999, and obtained a Juris Doctor degree from the University of Nevada, Las Vegas William S. Boyd School of Law in 2003. She began her career as a defense attorney, then worked as a litigation attorney for The Mirage from 2005 to 2008, served as city attorney for North Las Vegas from 2008 to 2016—becoming the first Black person to hold that position in Nevada—and later worked as director of external affairs for AT&T Services from 2016 to 2019. She joined the Nevada State Athletic Commission, the Nevada Gaming Commission, and in 2019 became chairwoman of the Nevada Gaming Control Board, appointed by Governor Steve Sisolak, making her the first Black chair. During her tenure, she introduced reforms, including a proposal requiring gaming companies to establish written policies against harassment and discrimination based on sex, race, color, gender identity, and national origin, and she oversaw the closing and reopening of casinos during the COVID-19 pandemic, while also serving on the State COVID-19 task force. After leaving the control board, she joined the boards of Caesars Entertainment, Fidelity National Financial, Inc., Allegiant Airlines, and Cerberus Cyber Sentinel. In November 2021, she joined the law firm Covington & Burling LLP as counsel and also operated her own consulting service, Douglass Morgan LLC. In December 2021, she was named vice chair of Las Vegas’ host committee for Super Bowl LVIII, scheduled for February 2024. On July 7, 2022, the Las Vegas Raiders announced her appointment as team president, making her the first Black and Asian female NFL team president and the third woman and third African-American in NFL history to become a team president. She is married to former Minnesota Vikings and Arizona Cardinals safety Don Morgan, and they have two children.
